related_questions.question: How long does it take to get COVID after being exposed?
related_questions.snippet: Key points. People with COVID-19 have a wide range of symptoms ranging from mild symptoms to severe illness. Symptoms may appear 2-14 days after exposure to the virus. Symptoms may start as mild, and some people will progress to more severe symptoms.
related_questions.title: Symptoms of COVID-19 - CDC

related_questions.question: What is the average incubation period for the current COVID variant?
related_questions.snippet: The COVID-19 incubation period is the time it takes for symptoms to develop after exposure to the virus. It typically ranges from two to 14 days, with an average time of 3-5 days. You can begin spreading the COVID virus during the incubation period, before you start having symptoms.
related_questions.title: COVID Incubation Period: Key Facts and Guidelines - Health

related_questions.question: How long after coming in contact with someone who has COVID should I get tested?
related_questions.snippet: If you have symptoms, test immediately, and then test again per the instructions if your first result is negative. If you were exposed to someone who has COVID-19 and you do not have symptoms, wait at least 5 full days after your exposure before testing. If you test too early, you may have an inaccurate result.

related_questions.question: How long after exposure to a virus do you get sick?

text_blocks.snippet: The time it takes to develop symptoms after exposure to a virus, known as the incubation period, varies greatly depending on the specific virus, but generally ranges from a few hours to several weeks. For example, the common cold can appear within 12 hours to three days, while other viruses like measles can take up to 21 days to manifest symptoms. COVID-19, for instance, typically shows symptoms between 2 and 14 days after exposure, with the omicron variant averaging three to four days.
